title: Expansion of Warehousing Station Designation
summary: The concept of a 'Warehousing Station' evolved from a general legal definition under the Customs Act to a specific administrative tool used to designate diverse economic zones and land customs stations. While the core legal definition remains anchored in Section 11 of the Customs Act, the application has shifted from a static regulatory category to an active policy instrument for extending customs-bonded facilities to specific economic zones and port infrastructure.

evolution.scope: Expanded from general customs jurisdiction to specific economic zones, land ports, and container terminals.
evolution.procedure: Shifted from automatic statutory recognition (in 2015 rules) to case-by-case NBR notification (in 2023/2024 SROs).

timeline.change: Formalized the automatic classification of Economic Zones and High-Tech Parks as Warehousing Stations.
Applied the designation to a specific land customs station (Sheola) via NBR notification.
Extended the designation to specific port infrastructure (Chittagong Port Authority facilities).

Warehousing Station: The National Board of Revenue has declared specific geographic areas as warehousing stations under the authority granted by Section 11 of the Customs Act 1969.

National Board of Revenue: The board is empowered by the Customs Act 1969 to formally notify and define the boundaries of customs warehousing stations.
